scope: Belica Void Drone actor and target-event recovery; not production integration
findings: The GA/GE/GMMC/GCN filename-selected corpus omitted the Drone actor Blueprint even though its raw asset was already extracted. Direct Blueprint class imports identify this dependency without re-extracting the game.

The authority-guarded actor path registers DroneUpdateTargets on a repeating timer with a serialized interval of approximately 0.15 seconds. It loops candidate targets and performs a line trace; the blocked branch removes GE_LtBelica_Drone_ManaDrain and the unblocked branch adds the target and applies that effect from the instigator ability system, with the Drone as source object.

The target ability listens for ability commits with AbilityType.Ability and for Event.OnDamaged. Its damage-event branch requires GameplayEffect.LtBelica.VoidDrone.TriggerDamage and equality between the event instigator and the instigator of the stored Drone damage spec.

FireDroneLaserAtTarget resolves the Drone from the granting context source object and requests a serialized approximately 0.1-second latent Delay before applying ZapDrain and the stored GE_DamageSpec to the target ability owner. It does not construct a fresh damage spec at this application site.
A separate approximately 0.01-second WaitDelay in activation ends in an execution-flow return; it must not be mistaken for automatic firing or the zap delay.

The legacy GrantedAbilities entry is null, but the exact AbilitiesGameplayEffectComponent GrantAbilityConfigs property grants GA_LtBelica_VoidDrone_Target_C. It binds level to VoidDrone_Level and records CancelAbilityImmediately removal policy. The stored policy alone does not certify cleanup; the separate native dispatch and end traces below establish the supported chain.

Native component reflection exposes GrantAbilityConfigs through GameplayAbilitySpecConfig, not the legacy GameplayAbilitySpecDef layout. The shared GameplayEffectComponent base has zero own reflected fields; this does not imply no native state or inherited defaults.

The exact ongoing-tag requirement on ManaDrain requires LtBelica.AbilityE.Drone.Dummy. The Dummy effect grants that tag, has Infinite duration, AggregateByTarget stacking and limit one. The actor volume now has a decoded Dummy-effect binding; normal native overlap application and removal are traced below.

The exact damage AssetTags component includes AbilityDamage, SpellVamp, TriggersSpellShield, AoE, Summon and Damage.Ability.Secondary tags. These are recovered properties, not tags inferred only from a name table.

The 274-entry KismetSystemLibrary registration table identifies the Delay thunk. Its supplied LatentActionInfo fields are used to look up a pending action by callback target and UUID. If an action is found, the path returns without allocating another or rewriting its remaining time; otherwise it stores the supplied duration and callback information in a new action.

Drone FireDroneLaserAtTarget uses the same serialized latent UUID and Self callback target for each call at that site. Pending repeated calls therefore coalesce for the same callback object; different callback objects are not automatically coalesced together.

The created delay action update subtracts the response time-step value and requests completion when the remaining value is nonpositive. This supports delayed/coalesced delivery, not a frame-exact timing guarantee.

The Drone actor PredGameplayVolume component has an exact FilterAndEffectsContainers property whose entry selects enemy heroes, excludes self/minions/structures/damageables, checks targetability, permits stealthed targets, and does not require line of sight. Its configured stacked effect is GE_LtBelica_Drone_ManaDrainDummy_C with StackCount one. This establishes the serialized presence-effect binding by itself; native overlap application/removal paths are traced separately below.

The volume component property stream reaches its end after 82 of 90 bytes; both recovered properties roundtrip exactly. Eight trailing bytes remain opaque. SnapshotSourceForPeriodicEffects is explicitly false; absent properties and inherited defaults have not been certified.

RemoveEnemy casts the departing actor to a hero and branches on CompareTeams result equal to byte one. On the selected branch it removes GE_LtBelica_Drone_ManaDrain_C with no instigator filter and stack count minus one, removes that hero from PossibleTargets, and stops tracking if it was CurrentTarget. The team enum label and native removal/cancellation effects are not inferred from the byte value.

Native reflection recovered the PredGameplayVolumeComponent and ActorComponent own field layouts plus fifteen dependent struct layouts. These are reusable schemas, not evidence of inherited default values or native lifecycle behavior.

Native normal volume entry filters targets, applies specs, and records successful effect handles. Repeated tracked overlaps increment the target count without repeating the normal immediate application. Normal exit removes recorded effects only after tracked overlap/reference counts are exhausted. This supports removal of the bound Dummy presence effect on normal exit, subject to runtime overrides and unresolved shared stacking.
The volume native constructor assigns automatic effect handling and enabled volume. These are constructor assignments, not proof that inherited archetypes or runtime code never override them.

The Drone target superclass is PredGameplayAbility. Its successful native end path queues latent-action removal keyed to that same ability object. Manager processing removes matching UUID/action pairs; the ordinary Delay abort handler does not execute the zap continuation. Effect-policy dispatch is traced separately below; same-frame expiry/removal ordering remains unresolved.

The named DisableGameplayVolume path disables the volume and removes recorded normal-effect handles. Its optional boolean controls clearing the tracking map, not whether the handles are removed. Destruction is not assumed to call this entry.

Deferred linked-overlap processing accumulates signed per-actor counts, then calls normal entry or exit callbacks. Net zero explicitly dispatches one entry followed by one exit. Exact dispatch time remains unresolved; a simulator must not simply discard net-zero transitions.

The Drone component template directly references the native default component, with no intervening Blueprint component archetype. Together with recovered constructor assignments and exact component properties, this supports initially enabled automatic handling, subject to later native initialization or runtime changes.

The effect-component OnActiveGameplayEffectRemoved callback reaches RemoveAbilities. The verified CancelAbilityImmediately policy dispatches ClearAbility; the PredAbilitySystemComponent removal override calls its base, which directly ends active ability instances. This bypasses the ordinary CancelAbility cancelability check and connects effect removal to the previously traced latent cleanup. Authority/spec prerequisites and scope-lock deferral still apply.

Native ongoing-tag requirement failure calls SetActiveGameplayEffectInhibit. Its state-change delegate is bound by the ability component: inhibition removes granted abilities via the recovered policy; uninhibition invokes its grant path. Thus losing the required Dummy tag can end the target ability and clear its pending zap, separately from explicit actor-exit effect removal. Inhibition is not full effect deletion; reactivation identity/timing and shared tag sources remain qualified.

Native owner application forwards the stored damage spec. The traced instant-effect spec-copy helper retains the context object and reference controller rather than minting a per-application identity. This supports shared identity through that boundary, not final Noxia damage-event identity. The packaged inherited Instant duration policy is corroborated by the subsequent parent/default recovery; runtime overrides remain possible.

Adding the already-decoded GE_AbilityDamageEffect parent schema resolves the prior inherited-index stop. Drone damage and parent CDO property streams end at 605/609 and 70/74 bytes with all recovered properties exact. Neither overrides DurationPolicy; verified native GameplayEffect constructor assignment and enum mapping establish the inherited packaged Instant policy. Four trailing bytes remain per stream.
limits: Timer dispatch order and same-frame expiry versus removal remain unresolved. Successful ability end queues latent cleanup; CancelAbilityImmediately uses ClearAbility to end active instances, with authority/spec prerequisites and scope-lock deferral.

Remaining actor defaults, overlap radius, destruction cleanup, cross-volume shared stacking and grant reactivation/instance identity still require recovery. Normal entry/exit, disable and linked-overlap processing are traced; runtime overrides remain possible.
Owner application and instant-spec copying preserve the stored context through the traced boundary; final damage-event/Noxia identity remains unverified.
No in-game measurement was made. Instruction byte agreement is not whole-asset/default/native certification.
Production still approximates Drone delivery as one immediate damage packet per damaging activation; this native recovery does not itself change Drone damage or live data.

Recovered effect-component and damage/default properties roundtrip exactly but retain four trailing bytes outside completed streams. Completion of property streams is not whole-asset or runtime-override certification.
next: Resolve grant reactivation/instance identity, destruction cleanup and stored-spec identity semantics for a bounded Drone event simulation.
Retain explicit assumptions for scope-lock deferral, shared stacking and boundary-frame ordering.
Integrate supported conditional hit delivery with explicit target/cast assumptions, Noxia identity and Combustion filters, then rebuild the comparison.
